name: Addiction
effect: The Protagonist is addicted to a substance. A week of withdrawal will cause a level of exhaustion every day which are not naturally regenerated anymore. Other exhaustion still regenerates naturally until two weeks of withdrawal. This only applies to uncontrolled withdrawal, not to therapy.

name: Agoraphobia (DC)
effect: The Protagonist is afraid of wide, open places.

name: Annoying Voice
effect: The Protagonist has an annoying voice. This grants -10 to social tests that involve talking.

name: Arrogance (DC)
effect: The Protagonist believes to be superior to others.

name: Backwoods Customs
effect: Even though most cultures have melted, the Protagonist has grown up outside the core of society. He has internalized customs that some would call barbaric.

name: Bad Reputation
effect: The Protagonist has some sort of bad reputation, either from well known deeds or from known genetic markers. If he is talking to someone who knows of this, he gains a penalty equal to 5 times the boon's level. Can be taken up to level 10.

name: Bathophobia (DC)
effect: The Protagonist is afraid of depths. This may trigger at the bottom of the ocean just as much as it could in a massive canyon.

name: Belief in Authority (DC)
effect: The Protagonist believes in authority and those who represent it. Not compatible with Rebel.

name: Berserk Rush
effect: When the Protagonist is thoroughly enraged or he is influenced by substances that boost courage, he falls into a frenzy. Restraint tests to resist frenzy suffer a -20.

name: Blind
effect: The Protagonist can't see. This is due to nervous or brain damage and can't be fixed via augments.

name: Blood Lust (DC)
effect: Lust for bloody combat drives the Protagonist. She likes taking the time to make her victims suffer and might end up causing trouble for herself and her group due to this.

name: Bound by Duty
effect: The Protagonist is obliged to follow a certain person's or group's commands. If she disobeys, there might be severe external consequences.

name: Bound by Principle
effect: The Protagonist is bound by her own principles. They are central moral values that may rarely be bent and almost never broken. If they are, doubts will follow the Protagonist for at least a week, inferring a -40 penalty to anything requiring focus. By the Adjudicator's discretion these penalties might function slightly differently depending on the situation.

name: Caring (DC)
effect: The Protagonist is overly caring for his peers. He will take great risks to help others.

name: Claustrophobia (DC)
effect: The Protagonist is afraid of small, narrow places.

name: Clumsy
effect: Critical failures occur on a roll of 96 and above.

name: Colorblind
effect: The Protagonist is incapable of seeing colors. When she wants to identify something that is only discernible by color, she takes a -20 penalty. This also counts for ranged attacks against large or smaller targets.

name: Curiosity (DC)
effect: When there is something to know, the Protagonist will want to know, whether it is of concern or not.

name: Cursed by Fortuna
effect: When a bad event hits the group, this Protagonist is much more likely to be hit in particular. Also once per session the Adjudicator may declare a success to be a failure instead.

name: Debt
effect: The Protagonist is indebted to someone. The loaner will require regular payments or favors, or the Protagonist will suffer consequences depending on their relationship and the type of people they are.

name: Delusions of Grandeur (DC)
effect: The Protagonist tends to overstate and overestimate her own ability and take on monumental tasks with delusional confidence.

name: Destitute
effect: The Protagonist has made some bad choices regarding their money. While not knee-deep in debt, she does not have fund and currently lives from paycheck to paycheck. She starts with only half the cash. Cannot be combined with Big Spender.

name: Dietary Rules
effect: The Protagonist will only eat certain things due to personal reasons. Whenever he is forced to eat something that does not align with his values, e.g. as to not starve to death, he will suffer general penalties of at least -30 resulting from guilt.

name: Directionally Challenged
effect: The Protagonist has extreme difficulty distinguishing left from right. This makes navigation quite difficult: Navigation (the Skill) and navigation-related tests - like tests made in a chase - are at a -10 and can never benefit from map data (like Roadware).

name: Dwarfish
effect: The Protagonist is tiny. He is harder to hit, has less melee range and is slower. He is also rarely taken seriously.

name: Envy (DC)
effect: When another has something that the Protagonist does not, she tends to overstep boundaries to get some of her own.

name: Evil Monologue
effect: The Protagonist tends to talk to herself. This may lead to embarrassing social encounters or even to spilling information about secret plans.

name: Fear of Heights (DC)
effect: The Protagonist is followed by an everlasting fear of falling.

name: Flimsy
effect: Medical Toughness reduced by 1. Can be taken multiple times.

name: Food Restrictions
effect: Due to mutation or specific engineering, the Protagonist can only consume certain types of food. Anything else leaves the body undigested; often times violently.

name: Forgetful
effect: The Protagonist tends to forget even the most important details. Any Education is twice as expensive.

name: Gambler (DC)
effect: The Protagonist will not pass up on a good bet. When he can play a more or less fair game for something, he has a hard time passing up the chance.

name: Greed (DC)
effect: Money makes the world go round. Opportunities to make your world go just that bit rounder are very hard to pass by.

name: Hallucinations
effect: Hallucinating Protagonists live in a notably vastly different reality, e.g. thinking that milk is a deadly poison, that he is haunted by demons only vulnerable to supersonic cheese and so on. Every person will notice and this will infer penalties as per the Adjudicator's discretion.

name: Hesitant
effect: The Protagonist suffers a -3 to initiative.

name: Hungry I/II/III
effect: The Protagonist needs 1.5/2/3 times as much food.

name: Impaired Sense
effect: One of the Protagonist's senses functions improperly, incurring -20 on checks based on that sense. This may be offset with augments but never restored to normal levels. Not compatible with Outstanding Sense for the same sense.

name: Impatient (DC)
effect: The Protagonist does not like waiting. Tasks that take a long time of not doing much will be severely harder.

name: Impulsive
effect: The Protagonist tends to act on stupid decisions in the heat of the moment. When such an idea comes up, it takes a -20 intelligence check to resist acting on it.

name: Insomnia
effect: Getting a good night's rest is hard for this Protagonist. In roughly half of all nights (whether randomly or following a pattern) he takes a -30 penalty to regenerating naturally.

name: Laziness (DC)
effect: The Protagonist is a slob and doesn't put more effort into things than absolutely necessary.

name: Light Sensitivity
effect: The Protagonist hates the light. Every action taken in light is at a -30 penalty. Sufficient protection from the light is generally enough work and requires enough equipment that the sheer bulk grants similar penalties.

name: Ignorant (DC)
effect: The Protagonist has a hard time understanding a certain topic. This topic should be specified when the Bane is chosen. All tests checking knowledge of that topic suffer a penalty equal to this disabling characteristic.

name: Naive (DC)
effect: The Protagonist easily trusts strangers. Resisting deception and persuasion is at a penalty equal to the Bane.

name: Necrophobia (DC)
effect: The Protagonist has fear of death and dead creatures and will be unable to focus properly when on battlefields, murder or slaughter scenes or graveyards.

name: Needy (DC)
effect: The Protagonist's strong physical desires often become distracting to everyday life. He has a hard time focussing around or resisting the wishes of attractive people.

name: Nervous
effect: Rayleigh Index reduced by 1. Can be taken multiple times.

name: Neurotically Hygienic (DC)
effect: The Protagonist has an obsessive need to keep clean.

name: Night Blind
effect: Doubles all penalties for low light.

name: No Tactile Sense
effect: Anything requiring sense of touch takes a -40 penalty, this includes the usage of any weapon with a trigger or a blade.

name: Nyctophobia (DC)
effect: The Protagonist has a strong fear of the dark.

name: Obese
effect: The Protagonist is heavily overweight. This comes with multiple drawbacks like a -20 penalty to strength based checks that have to do with body weight (e.g. climbing), -3 to medical toughness, as well as stigmatization and other drawbacks by the Adjudicator's discretion.

name: One-Armed
effect: The Protagonist has lost an arm and due to nerve damage can't accept replacements.

name: One-Eyed
effect: The Protagonist has lost an eye and due to nerve damage can't accept replacements.

name: One-Handed
effect: The Protagonist has lost a hand and due to nerve damage can't accept replacements.

name: One-Legged
effect: The Protagonist has lost a leg and due to nerve damage can't accept replacements.

name: Paralyzed Leg
effect: Due to irreversible nervous damage the Protagonist can barely move one leg. This reduces speed by 2 and grants penalties around -15 to tests as per the Adjudicator's discretion.

name: Personal Enemy
effect: An important person or group has set its eyes on the Protagonist and will take measures to foil his plans.

name: Physically Repulsive
effect: The Protagonist is staggeringly ugly. This infers a -20 penalty to social tests when the Protagonist can be seen. Not compatible with Smoking, Looker and Ugly.

name: Playful (DC)
effect: The Protagonist loves playing. That can include simple things like chess or video games, but also "games" of predator and prey.

name: Portly
effect: The Protagonist is stocky or otherwise slower than her peers. Her speed is reduced by 1.

name: Prejudice (DC)
effect: The Protagonist is biased against a certain group of people and has a hard time interacting with them.

name: Rebel (DC)
effect: The Protagonist has a hard time trusting authority and tends to revolt. Not compatible with Belief in Authority.

name: Righteous (DC)
effect: Some laws are absolute and they must be followed. The Protagonist will work against any injustice to the order she believes in.

name: Scrooge (DC)
effect: Spending money is painful.

name: Second-class Citizen
effect: The Protagonist is oppressed for one reason or another. This may e.g. be due to stigmatization of a part of his lifestyle or being born with extremely few resources. In any case this will have consequences in social situations and encounters with law enforcement. Cannot be taken by Vat-grown.

name: Sensitive Smell (DC)
effect: When around something that smells particularly nasty, he takes penalties to everything that requires concentration or a healthy stomach.

name: Short
effect: The Protagonist is small. He is harder to hit, has less melee range and is slower. He is also rarely taken seriously.

name: Shortcoming
effect: A characteristic, that hasn't been invested in, is reduced by 5.

name: Sickly
effect: Grants -15 penalty to resist disease.
note: \begin{exampleblock} Banes like \emph{Sickly} may have no chance to come up in game. In this case such Banes should be disallowed by the Adjudicator.\end{exampleblock}

name: Slave Mentality (DC)
effect: The Protagonist does not like making his own decisions - such situations put a lot of stress on him. He is instead likely to adopt an idea ushered by someone else.

name: Slow Healer
effect: The Protagonist only heals naturally at a -20 penalty and tests taken to heal this Protagonist are at a -10.

name: Speech Disorder
effect: The Protagonist has some sort of speaking disorder. What it may be, he suffers a -10 to tests requiring to speak and takes longer to finish sentences which might cause problems in stressful situations like combat or a heated chase.

name: Split Consciousness
effect: Multiple consciousnesses fight over control of a single body. The Protagonist is represented by multiple character sheets (and generally multiple Voices), sharing physical characteristics, boons and banes, health conditions and their Athletics level. Mental characteristics boons and banes, conditions and all other skills are individual to every consciousness.

name: Squeamish (DC)
effect: The Protagonist takes a penalty to tests to resist fear and panic.

name: Superstition (DC)
effect: The Protagonist is superstitious, often believing ideas that depend on far fetched assumptions.

name: Technophobia (DC)
effect: The Protagonist is suspicious of technological advancements, especially solutions to things that could easily be done by humans.

name: Temperamental (DC)
effect: Small things may make the Protagonist unreasonably angry.

name: Terrible Odor
effect: The Protagonist has bad smell. This grants -10 to social tests when the Protagonist is in smelling distance and hiding from watchdogs is essentially impossible. Not compatible with Pleasant smell.

name: Trigger Phrase
effect: Sleeper agents were rumored to have trigger phrases carved into their mind. For the longest time that was purely a myth but now many vat-grown are programmed with such a phrase to force certain behavior. When the phrase is heard by the Protagonist, all tests to resist persuasion and commands suffer at least a -40 penalty.

name: Trouble Magnet (DC)
effect: Some people actively look for trouble. This Protagonist has the tendency, willingly or not, to provoke and attract the wrath of others.

name: Ugly
effect: The Protagonist is unshapely. This grants -10 to social tests while the Protagonist is being seen. Not compatible with Smoking, Looker and Physically repulsive.

name: Uneducated
effect: The Protagonist has not learned much - he loses 50 XP. Can be taken multiple times, but XP may never be negative.

name: Vanity (DC)
effect: The Protagonist is posh to an extreme. He might refuse tube food, simple and cheap clothing or getting dirty.

name: Vengeful (DC)
effect: The Protagonist does not forget, nor does he forgive. When someone wronged him, he will make sure to pay them back tenfold.

name: Wanted I-V
effect: The Protagonist is being looked for by an organization. This can be due to criminal record, corporate espionage or involvement in gang wars. The first step roughly describes being the target of a small mercenary or criminal group, a level 3 target would be a low-priority military target and a level 5 target is on LEGION's radar.
